samples.summary: Fix report is now posted before the push, so the author's "FIXED" claim can exist on the PR for code that never lands
samples.evidence: The prompt now orders the fix report before the `git push` (`.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml:1665-1680`, reinforced at :1729-1734). The report is an AUTHOR CLAIM channel that feeds the adjudicator — the one component allowed to remove a finding from the merge gate (`scripts/agent/fix-report.mjs:266-345`, `authorClaims` → `toRebuttalRecords`). Previously a report could only exist after a successful push, so every "I fixed this" claim was backed by code that actually reached the branch. With the new ordering, a fixer whose push is denied, killed mid-hook (`--no-verify` timeout path, :1743-1754), or otherwise never lands still leaves a `fixed` record on the PR; `latestReport`/`authorClaims` (fix-report.mjs:233-285) select it purely by comment order and never compare `report.head` against the sha actually under review (only loop-status.mjs:285 does a head match, and only for display). A later round (a human push, `@claude fix`, or a re-run) would then hand up to MAX_FIX_ADJUDICATIONS=5 unbacked "the author reports it FIXED this" prompts to the adjudicator. Chain stops short of an exploit: `toRebuttalRecords` frames the claim as unproven, `isOverturningVerdict` still requires the adjudicator's own file:line grounding, the author gate `fromRebuttalAuthor` (rebuttal.mjs:224-228) keeps outsiders out of the channel, and the "Page if the fix produced no commit" step (:1806) pages when nothing was pushed. So this is claim/evidence-ordering hardening rather than a demonstrated bypass — the safe form would be for the panel to ignore a report whose `head` does not correspond to a dispatch whose commit actually landed.
